highlights.title: Giving AI a “crystal clear” view of the materials world
highlights.summary: New research can help AI models understand crystalline materials in 3D and reason about their properties.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."

In principle, artificial intelligence could make finding the right material for an application as simple as ordering dinner: Scientists would tell a large language model what they want, and it would serve them a perfectly designed crystal for the job.

Unfortunately, that approach doesn’t work well yet, and the problem comes down to data: Most materials consist of crystals, which are 3D periodic arrangements of atoms whose structures are stored in specialized formats, not the text streams that today’s large language models are trained on. The experimental literature is also heavily biased toward a few popular classes of crystals, making AI outputs skew toward those materials.

highlights.title: Stephen King and Stanley Kubrick's Near-Perfect Psychological Thriller Is Officially Back on Streaming
highlights.summary: Stephen King is a vocal guy. The Master of Horror has published over 65 novels and novellas, countless short stories, and five nonfiction books since the mid-’70s. The hype that surrounds him is well deserved.
body: The Shining, published in 1977, is one of King’s most personal works. The novel follows Jack Torrance, a struggling writer who takes a job as the caretaker of a cursed hotel. There, he slowly loses his mind and puts his family in danger. King has called the novel a reflection of his own struggles with alcoholism and fears related to parenting.

Three years later, it was adapted into a movie. Stanley Kubrick’s The Shining is one of the most enduring works of horror in cinema history. It’s nihilistic and cold, and one of the best showcases of Kubrick’s omnipotent camera. King is famously not a fan.

Jack Torrance (Jack Nicholson) is an aspiring novelist and former teacher who takes a job as the caretaker for the Overlook Hotel in the Colorado Rockies. He moves there with his wife Wendy (Shelley Duvall) and their son Danny (Danny Lloyd) as the hotel closes for the winter season.

Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”

highlights.title: ‘We hang on to summer a little longer here’: five of the best places for autumn sun in Europe and Turkey
highlights.summary: If you’re looking for a last blast of summer, these sunny resorts offer quiet beaches but enough life to stave off the end-of-season blues. A Kalkan sunset is always a beautiful thing – the horseshoe-shaped bay deepening to azure blue against an apricot-rose sky – but, in October, when the light is…
body: For me, the best thing about an autumn break – besides the sunsets – is that I can visit some of my favourite places that just get overrun in summer. The glittering beach at Kaputas, sandwiched into a triangular gap on the mountainous Kalkan-Kas road, has become a victim of Instagram; from May to September, it’s impossible to get near. In October, the waters are still warm and the beach – although still busy – has plenty of space for a dip and a laze.

About 20 minutes’ drive inland, the mountain village of Bezirgan, which used to serve as a summer retreat for wealthier Kalkan residents, settles back into complete peace in autumn, save for the woodpeckers battering away at the bark of the almond trees and the squirrels skittering through the leaves. The Lycian Way weaves through the village, past Ottoman-era grain stores, with the lush gardens of the Pirha Köy Sofrası restaurant a great bet for a plate of traditional manti (dumplings in yoghurt) or kofte (meatballs), before setting off for a hike (they do fantastic breakfasts too).

highlights.title: 60 Years Ago, the Best Charlie Brown Quote Was So Perfect It Made It Into the Movie
highlights.summary: Lucy’s quote, “Happiness is a warm puppy,” is another great one that touches on life’s simple joys on a really deep level. But to determine the best quote ever uttered by Charlie Brown, I didn't want accidental brilliance, I wanted something that he understands as much as the audience does.
body: Many of the best Peanuts quotes involve a character saying something accidentally brilliant. While a line might be intentionally insightful when it was written by creator Charles Schulz, when those words transfer from his mind to the mouths of his creations, it's usually without ever meaning to say anything brilliant — or even notice they did. For example, the best line about heartbreak from Peanuts is “Nothing takes the taste out of peanut butter like unrequited love!” That quote perfectly encapsulates the physiological sensation associated with romantic rejection, but for Charlie Brown, he’s just reacting to the feeling without any deeper intention.

highlights.title: Ryan Gosling’s Zero-G Stunts on ‘Project Hail Mary’ Broken Down by the Space Epic’s VFX Supervisors
highlights.summary: For Oscar-winning VFX supervisor Paul Lambert Lambert, of all the huge challenges presented by Ryan Gosling space epic “Project Hail Mary,” the most daunting was creating convincing zero gravity.
body: “Zero-G was probably my personal biggest concern going into the movie,” he said at View Conference in Turin, Italy, drilling down on its VFX.

Other experiments were deliberately hands-on. Fraser used an infrared-modified camera, programmable IR lights and water running in front of the lens to develop some of the film’s stranger imagery. “It was literally a mad science lab,” Lambert recalled. Burning fireballs, liquids, lasers and ferrofluid were also filmed to provide starting points for the microscopic effects.

The DP returned during postproduction to work with ILM’s Helios virtual-camera system on the sequence near Adrian. Artists tracked Gosling’s on-set performance and recreated it within digital environments, allowing Fraser to choose new camera positions without discarding the original acting.

Across those techniques, the supervisors’ ambition remained consistent: to make even the most elaborate effects obey a recognizable physical logic while ensuring Rocky felt as present beside Gosling as any human scene partner.

highlights.title: My longterm boyfriend died last year. Is it too soon to date someone new? | Ask Annalisa Barbieri
highlights.summary: Only you can know when you are ready, but a year is not long to process grief, and you seem to have doubts about this man. My long term boyfriend died of cancer last year. We’d been together for 16 years, since I was 21 and he was 23.
body: I loved my late partner deeply and had planned to stay with him for ever. We were embarking on an 18-year project together, raising our son. Now I think, how can I ever be happy again?

Before he died, my partner told me to find a single dad to go out with. When I returned to work, a colleague I had considered a flirt was away – getting chemo. Now he’s in remission. He’s also a single parent. Lately, I’ve realised I have a crush on him. His life has been touched by tragedy and he knows what’s important to him. He’s very kind, like my late partner, and I think we click.

What gives me a lot of pause is that I find him to blow hot and cold. Also, because I’m a solo mum I don’t really have time for someone else. But he has recently left the company, so I wouldn’t be dating a co-worker.
I s it remarkable to meet a single dad you genuinely like? Or are there more out there than I think? Please tell me what you think I should do.
points: Only you can know when you are ready, but a year is not long to process grief, and you seem to have doubts about this man.

highlights.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
highlights.summary: After backlash, Meta is updating its terms again to remove language that suggested it could scrape content from sites, including news sites, to train its AI. Specifically, the following language no longer appears on the commercial terms page: … Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages…
body: Language that experts say allowed the scraping of news sites to train its AI has been removed from Meta’s terms.

Many, including Neiman Lab and James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell, interpreted it as an attempt to give Meta the right to use content scraped from sites to train its AI products for free and supersede blocking instructions in a site’s robots.txt file.

“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves. It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers. As always, content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences. This is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don’t give us new rights that supersede those preferences.”

highlights.title: Every Major Game Releasing in November That Isn’t GTA 6
highlights.summary: For millions of gamers, November is all about one video game: Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar’s much-anticipated open-world crime game is likely to spark a cultural moment that we haven’t seen in games since Animal Crossing: New Horizons in 2020.
body: The good news for anyone looking for some good GTA 6 counter-programming is that there are more games coming out next month. While it’s not as crowded a field as we typically get in November, there’s still sure to be something for you. Here’s a look at some of the highlights you can expect to play if you’re avoiding the streets of Vice City.

In a crowded Gamescom Opening Night Live stream, Gravhounds was a real attention-grabber. The upcoming co-op shooter puts you and your friends in control of gun-toting dogs forced to shoot their way through an alien planet. With base building mechanics and some gravity-bending physics to toy with, it could wind up being a goofy multiplayer hit. It’s set to launch into early access starting on Nov. 2.

Anyone who grew up in the GameCube era will no doubt remember Godzilla: Destroy All Monster Melee, if only for its iconic cover art. 24 years after its release, the cult classic kaiju brawler is returning in a freshly remastered form complete with online multiplayer. If you’ve never played it, don’t sleep on it: It’s a surprisingly fun casual fighting game that’s filled with classic monsters.

highlights.title: Going nowhere fast? Personal trainers on why you aren’t seeing results in the gym
highlights.summary: From doing too much cardio to wasting time – PTs reveal the common fails stunting your progress, and how to avoid them. We’ve all done it. Launched ourselves head first into a new regime – perhaps as the result of a new year resolution, recent breakup or aggressively unflattering photo.
body: A better approach is to devise a realistic training schedule that actually aligns with your lifestyle. “When getting started, lower the bar,” she suggests. “Aim for two weekly strength sessions done consistently. If you manage that, and have the time, energy and inclination to do more, you can always add in a third. It’s much easier to build on something you’re doing consistently than repeatedly start over with something that’s unsustainable.”

“There’s an outdated belief that you must ‘keep the body guessing’ in order for it to adapt, by continually switching up your workouts,” says Nick Finney, who has trained Robbie Williams and Jennifer Lopez. “I understand that people want to avoid boredom by changing what they do each workout, but it ends up hindering their progress. You need to practise your technique, become more proficient and give your body time to improve and get stronger. If you keep changing things up, then it’s impossible to measure progress by comparing what you achieved in previous workouts.”

highlights.title: OpenAI is building a humanoid robot, but the body isn't the real challenge
highlights.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wants a humanoid that can operate in a world designed for people, though the CEO says a robot 'brain' is a much bigger challenge.
body: Figuring out how the 'brain' will work will take a lot of time.
While OpenAI is already busy with the development of AI models and new consumer hardware, CEO Sam Altman and his team apparently have time for one more project: a humanoid robot.

On the Sources podcast, Altman explained that the human form is logical because "the world is very much designed for people." Doors, keyboards and tools are all designed around a certain type of body, and a robot that can move around in the same spaces should probably have a similar form factor. As Altman put it, "matching that form factor seems good."

When asked if OpenAI will actually build one, his response was much more succinct: "We will." However, Altman isn't so concerned with the nitty-gritty details of what that robot looks like. Those questions are "less important than really figuring out... the brain that makes the robot work," he said. Basically, giving a machine two arms and two legs doesn't get you very far if it doesn't know what to do with them.

highlights.summary: Updates as the Proteas host Australia at St George’s Park. Play start time in Gqeberha is 10am local/7pm AEDT/9am BST. Any thoughts? Get in touch with an email. I like all the changes for South Africa.
body: I like all the changes for South Africa. It’s great that Tristan Stubbs wants to be a Test player, given all his attention from the franchise circuit, but he didn’t look up to speed in Durban, where Breetzke really did take it up to the Aussies in the one-day series, and looked to have a lot to offer technically as well as in attitude.

Ackerman has a monster first-class record and has earned a shot at the next level up, and to make space for him the move involved getting Rickelton out of the opening spot, which he desperately needs based on the evidence of Durban, then having him go down the order to become the keeper in place of Verreyne, who was dreadful last start and hasn’t made runs in any Test for a while.

Then Rabada coming in speaks for itself, although Maharaj has historically taken the fight up to the Australians, so I’d have expected him to stay as the lone spinner. But glad to see Harmer get another chance to show his quality.
So the hosts look stronger up top, stronger in the middle, and stronger as a bowling outfit. It may all fail terribly, but it’s a nice setup before a ball is bowled.

body: Directed and co-written by James Cameron, The Terminator, which is currently free to stream on YouTube (with ads), is the story of two opposing time travelers from the year 2029 who venture back to the year 1984 to the city of Los Angeles. The first of these time travelers is a robot (Schwarzenegger) with living tissue over its body. Called a “Terminator,” the robot is a killing machine sent back to murder a woman named Sarah Connor (Linda Hamilton). In the future, the world is controlled by machines, but Sarah’s son John Connor will become the leader of the human resistance, which causes so much trouble for the machines that they send the Terminator back to eliminate him before he is born.
The other time traveler is Kyle Reese (Michael Biehn), a trusted soldier in the human resistance who is sent back in time by John to protect his mother from the Terminator.

highlights.title: How The Traitors' music plays with your emotions
highlights.summary: It's not just treachery and villainy - the soundtrack for Traitors helps set the show's campy tone.
body: Have you ever noticed how the soundtrack manipulates your perception? A sinister orchestral flourish hints at a double cross. A cheeky chord injects humour into a kitchen conflab.
As ever, though, you shouldn't trust what happens in the castle. The music can provide emphasis or act as misdirection, all at the producers' behest.

"I remember the BBC was quite reluctant to even think about a show with murder as a main feature, so I knew I didn't want the music to go really dark," says Sam Watts, who composed the opening theme and much of the incidental score (but is not responsible for the show's haunting cover versions of well-known pop songs... more on those later).

Watts, who had previously worked on Planet Earth and The Sarah Jane Adventures, pitched to work on the programme with only a basic idea of the set-up. It was only when he learned Winkleman was the host that he settled on his approach.

highlights.title: Mercedes-AMG’s first ground-up SUV is a 1,150hp electric beast
highlights.summary: Earlier this year, Mercedes' AMG performance brand grabbed our attention with the GT four-door coupe, a souped-up sports sedan with three axial flux motors delivering over 1,150 horsepower.
body: It may even out-muscle the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric and Lucid Gravity.

The AMG GT SUV (say that five times fast) marks the first time in the performance brand’s 59-year history that it has developed a full-size SUV entirely in-house from the ground up. Scheduled to hit the US next summer, the new EV is built on Merc’s high-performance AMG.EA architecture to combine sports-car handling with full-size SUV suburban practicality.

It will be available in three trims — GT 53, GT 55, and the flagship GT 63 — with the top model delivering 1,153hp via the same three axial flux motors powering the four-door coupe. That beats the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric with Launch Control, which is sure to make for some awkward run-ins around Stuttgart.

Thanks to an 800-volt architecture, the SUV supports blistering-fast charging speeds up to 710kW on the 128kWh battery (GT 63 / GT 55) and 600kW on the 106kWh battery (GT 53). Drivers can charge 10–80 percent in 12 minutes or gain up to 450km (around 280 miles) of WLTP range in just 10 minutes. The 128kWh battery trims will have an estimated max range of 435 miles.

highlights.title: New Zealand avoid World Cup shock against Fiji
highlights.summary: New Zealand women are given a World Cup "wake-up call" after they are forced to come from behind to beat debutants Fiji in their opening game.
body: The Ferns are one of the most successful teams in women's rugby league history – they have reached the final of all six World Cups, winning the first three before finishing runners up to Australia in the previous three years.
They are generally considered second favourites this time around and were expected to win easily against the Fijians in Newcastle on Sunday.
Instead, New Zealand were made to battle to an 18-12 win, having trailed 12-4 in the first half.
They were 12-10 down at the break – the first time they have ever been behind at half-time in a World Cup match.

Players will also be able to turn the body shape changes "on" and "off" (and lock the shape) based on their preferences.

Gust: "When the feature is turned ON, Karia’s body shape will change depending on how much she eats during snacks. When it is turned OFF, her body shape will not change no matter how much she eats. "Whether you want to enjoy seeing Karia’s body shape change, keep your favorite body shape, or play without any body shape changes at all, the feature is being designed so you can enjoy the game in the way you prefer."

Koei Tecmo also surveyed fans about the best costumes for Karia and asked what kind of "special short story" based on a theme they should create, with "Karia goes on a food tour" taking out the top spot. You can see the other results on the official game site.

highlights.title: Why Britain should reject the lure of cheap – and scary – Chinese AI
highlights.summary: In the west the technology comes with at least some effort to provide security and a benign intent – not so from China. There is much to fear from artificial intelligence developed in China and handed to businesses and governments in the west almost free of charge.
body: Every month Chinese AI developers such as DeepSeek and Xiaomi dispatch the latest versions of their “open-weight” models that allow users to take the core software and use it without paying an expensive ongoing licence.
In Britain, we love cheap Chinese kit, usually setting aside any concerns about how it was made and who by.

The row over whether to allow Chinese electric cars unfettered access to British retail forecourts is a case in point. They are cheaper than other EVs sold in the UK and, consumers ask: What is not to like? These same consumers might consider how Chinese EVs are subsidised by Beijing deliberately to boost exports and, in so doing, undermine foreign domestic car industries.
It’s scary because Beijing is entering a new phase in the long march of economic development, taking the world’s second largest economy closer to making China great again.
points: In the west the technology comes with at least some effort to provide security and a benign intent – not so from China.
There is much to fear from artificial intelligence developed in China and handed to businesses and governments in the west almost free of charge.

highlights.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
highlights.summary: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes.
body: OpenAI, Meta, and Google want AI agents to do everything for you. But popular services on the web aren’t letting that happen.

In recent weeks, users of services like Meta’s Muse, xAI’s Grok, OpenAI’s Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. Yelp told TechCrunch that it only allows AI agents that pay for its data licensing program, while Delta Air Lines is preventing them from booking tickets on behalf of users. JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab have also confirmed that they’re blocking AI agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns. Some users say sites that previously worked with their AI agent are no longer accessible, including Cars.com and Amtrak, suggesting other companies could be quietly blocking them.

highlights.title: Dev Behind Russian Roulette Drinking Game Cancels Steam Demo Plans Following AI Copycat Concerns
highlights.summary: The developer behind Russian roulette anime game Drunken Goddess Reflux has canceled its plans for a public Steam demo, citing concerns over potential AI copycats. Alliance Arts and Who You's path to launch has seemingly been mostly bump-free since it was announced back in April.
body: Part of that release date announcement included the promise that a demo would launch October 19, but as explained in an update post on Steam, those plans have changed. What was originally intended to be a public release for the Drunken Goddess Reflux demo has now been canceled in favor of a "closed play session for a limited number of participants." It's a last-minute move Alliance Arts apologized for, but its concerns related to rapidly advancing AI technology were simply too great to ignore.

"We are concerned that, based on the content of the demo, works imitating or replicating this game's presentation and gameplay could be quickly produced using AI or other tools and released ahead of the game's launch," the developers said in their list of concerns.

In other words, sending a demo out into the wild could open the door for nefarious individuals to use AI to generate a low-effort clone or copycat experience. For a team hoping for a successful launch in just a few months, someone coming in to steal its thunder could potentially throw a wrench into things.
